entries.title: What a month in Oaxaca cost, peso by peso

fields.author: Ilse Varga
fields.standfirst: Rent, a desk, food, buses and a phone plan: the whole of October in Jalatlaco, to the peso.
fields.image_alt: What a month in Oaxaca cost, peso by peso (placeholder)
fields.body:
I arrived in Oaxaca on Oct 7, 2026 with a plan to stay two months and a budget I had guessed at from a friend's notes. This is what October actually came to, from the flat to the SIM card, with the receipts sorted on the kitchen table.

The short version: 24,750 MXN for the month. Rent was more than half of it. Food was the line I got most wrong, in a good way: the market in Jalatlaco fed me well for less than I spent in Mexico City.

Rent and the flat

A one-bedroom in Jalatlaco cost 14,500 a month, two months paid up front. It has a desk by the window, a gas boiler that wants a match and a roof where the Wi-Fi still holds. I found it through the owner of the coworking space, not a listing site.

Work, food and getting around

The desk at the shared studio off the zócalo was 2,800 for the month, and worth it for the calls alone. Food came to 6,200: market lunches most days and dinner out a couple of nights a week. Colectivos and the odd taxi home in the rain added 900, and a local SIM with data another 350.

Next time I would book the flat for the full two months from the start and skip the first week's guesthouse. Everything else I would do the same way. If something here has changed when you go, write to me and I will update the post.
fields.image_caption: The receipts, sorted by category on the kitchen table.

fields.verdict: Opens like a suitcase, carries like a backpack. The one thing I would buy again first.
One for work, one for clothes, one for things that charge.
Wear one, wash one, one spare. They forgive a week in a hot flat.
Packs to the size of a fist and has been used in every city.
Big enough to design on, small enough for a café table.
Saves my neck. Folds flatter than a notebook.
Goes with the stand. Typing on a raised laptop is miserable without it.
The office door I carry. Worth their weight on every bus.
One SIM, every device, and a network I trust in a flat I do not.
Charges the laptop, the phone and the router from one plug.
A full laptop charge for days when the power goes, which is more often than you think.
Every socket I have met so far, with two USB ports on the back.
Covers working abroad, billed monthly, cancellable any time.
Holds four currencies and pays in the local one without a fee.
Data on landing, before I find a shop for a local SIM.
For bank logins on café Wi-Fi, and nothing more exciting.
Letters at home are opened, scanned and emailed. Nothing gets lost.

/privacy.title: Privacy
/privacy.content:
This site sets one item in your browser's storage when you close the announcement or the notice, so they stay closed. It has no analytics, no tracking pixels and no advertising.

If you write through the contact form or join the postcards list, your email address is kept only to reply or to send the postcards. Unsubscribe from any postcard in one click, or write and I will delete what I hold.

Questions about this note go to hello@ilsevarga.example.

seo.description: What this site keeps about you, which is very little.
